post.description:
creates a filter/segment

Example Post Data:
{
    "name": "My Filter",
    "operator": "OR",
    "rules": [
        { "field":"email", "logic":"contains", "condition":"@gotham.com" },
        { "field":"activated", "logic":"bg", "condition":"1234567" },
        { "field":"firstname", "logic":"eq", "condition":"bruce" },
        { "field":"lastname", "logic":"eq", "condition":"wayne" }
    ]
}
Possible Operators
  1. OR
  2. AND (default)

Available Logics:
  1. eq - equals
  2. neq - not equals
  3. sm - smaller
  4. bg - bigger
  5. isnull - is empty
  6. notisnull - not empty
  7. contains - contains given string
  8. begins - begins with
  9. ends - ends with
  10. ismale - given field is male
  11. isfemale - given field is female

general available fields:
  1. email - (email of the receiver)
  2. source - (import source of the email)
  3. imported - (timestamp of receiver import)
  4. registered - (timestamp of receiver registration)
  5. activated - (timestamp of receiver activation)
  6. deactivated - (timestamp of receiver deactivation)
  7. bounced - (timestamp of receiver bounce)
  8. points - (points of the receiver)
  9. last_location - (last location of receiver)
  10. last_client - (last mail client used by receiver)
  11. crevent_mail_send (logic: eq, condition: mailing_id -> receiver of certain mailing)
  12. crevent_mail_open (logic: eq, condition: mailing_id -> opened mail of certain mailing)
  13. crevent_mail_click (logic: eq, condition: mailing_id -> clicked on mail of certain mailing)
  14. crevent_mail_bounce (logic: eq, condition: mailing_id -> bounced mail of certain mailing)
  15. all attributes (if global and group attributes have the same name, group ones will be favoured)

post.description:
create a new receiver

Carefully use the fields 'registered', 'activated' and 'deactivated':

- provide 'registered' with current time if receiver is new.
- provide 'activated' only for immedite activation (no DOI mail will work then).
- provide 'deactivated' other than 0 and your receiver will definitely be inactive.

Omission of all of those fields leads to an activated receiver ('registered' and 'activated' to current time)!

Example Post Data:
{
    "email":"bruce@gotham.com",
    "registered": "1118354400",
    "activated": "1118354400", // omit if receiver is to be activated later, e.g. DOI mail
    "deactivated": "0", // omit field unless you know what you are doing!
    "source":"Batcave Computer",
    "attributes": {
        "is_batman":"1"
    },
    "global_attributes": {
        "firstname":"Bruce",
        "lastname":"Wayne"
    },
    "tags": [ "hero", "rich", "smart" ],
    "orders": [
        {
            "order_id": "xyz123412",
            "product_id": "SN9876543",
            "product": "Batman - The Movie (DVD)",
            "price": 9.99,

            "quantity": 1,
            "mailing_id": "12345678"
        },

            "order_id": "xyz123411",
            "product_id": "SN9876542",

            "price": 9.99,
            "currency": "EUR",
            "quantity": 1,
            "mailing_id": "12345678"
        }
    ]
}

post.description:
adds given tags to receiver

only allowed characters are /[a-zA-Z0-9_\\-\\p{L}]+/u
that's basicly all latin characters including a few kyrilic ones
all other characters are replaces by underscore.

You can prefix an origin to a tag with a following period. Example: origin.tagname
The following rules apply to tag origins:
- everything before the first found period is considered an origin
- it is cut to 50 characters length
- it may use the same characterset as a tag
- it may be used multiple times of course (see example)

Example post Data:
{
  "tags": ["batman.Good",batman.DarkKnight","joker.evil","joker.fakeSmile","robin","alfred"],

}

get.summary: Get all bounces for your account. 🔐
get.description:
returns a list with all bounces for your account

We categorize bounces according to the messages from the receiving mailserver:

Categories (exerpt):
- permanent/hardbounce: mailbox does not exist
- softbounce: temporary errors
- blocked: receiving mailserver didn't accept our email
- delayed: temporary delivery error
- spam: receiving mailserver categorized your email as spam

There are also two types of bounces:
- type: mailing -- bounce was created through a mailing
- type: doi -- bounce was created while sending the DOI emails (form signup)
type_id is either the mailing id or the form id depending on the type

Example response data:
{
  "email": "batman@gotham.com",
  "category": "hardbounce",
  "occurences": 1,
  "last_update": 1595229122,
  "last_update_gmt": "2020-07-20T07:12:02+00:00",
  "expires_by": 1626855819,
  "expires_by_gmt": "2021-07-21T08:23:39+00:00",
  "bounce_message": "smtp; 550 Recipient does not exist",
  "type": "doi",
  "type_id": "12345678"
},


The pagesize is limited to 500. To get more, retrieve another page.
